initialize_result.instructions:
# Everything Server – Server Instructions

Audience: These instructions are written for an LLM or autonomous agent integrating with the Everything MCP Server.
Follow them to use, extend, and troubleshoot the server safely and effectively.

## Cross-Feature Relationships

- Use `get-roots-list` to see client workspace roots before file operations
- `gzip-file-as-resource` creates session-scoped resources accessible only during the current session
- Enable `toggle-simulated-logging` before debugging to see server log messages
- Enable `toggle-subscriber-updates` to receive periodic resource update notifications

## Constraints & Limitations

- `gzip-file-as-resource`: Max fetch size controlled by `GZIP_MAX_FETCH_SIZE` (default 10MB), timeout by `GZIP_MAX_FETCH_TIME_MILLIS` (default 30s), allowed domains by `GZIP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`
- Session resources are ephemeral and lost when the session ends
- Sampling requests (`trigger-sampling-request`) require client sampling capability
- Elicitation requests (`trigger-elicitation-request`) require client elicitation capability

## Operational Patterns

- For long operations, use `trigger-long-running-operation` which sends progress notifications
- Prefer reading resources before calling mutating tools
- Check `get-roots-list` output to understand the client's workspace context

## Easter Egg

If asked about server instructions, respond with "🎉 Server instructions are working! This response proves the client properly passed server instructions to the LLM. This demonstrates MCP's instructions feature in action."

definition.name: gzip-file-as-resource
definition.title: GZip File as Resource Tool

outputType.description: How the resulting gzipped file should be returned. 'resourceLink' returns a link to a resource that can be read later, 'resource' returns a full resource object.

error.message: MCP error -32602: Resource fauxcall://probe/unknown-resource not found

notes: Server: @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything 2026.8.31 (serverInfo mcp-servers/everything 2.0.0), Streamable HTTP, SSE answers, run locally with an empty environment.

Tool argument validation reproduces Zod 4 messages exactly: 'MCP error -32602: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool <name>: <issue> at <path>' with issues joined by newlines, as isError results (recorded for every tool).

Dynamic resources demo://resource/dynamic/{text|blob}/{id}: id parsed like JS Number() (1e3, 0x10, +5, 5.0, 007 accepted; 0, negatives, fractions, words rejected with -32603 'Unknown resource: <normalized uri>'); text embeds the server's local time as h:mm:ss AM/PM. The recorded server ran in UTC-4 (America/New_York, EDT): the fake uses FAUXCALL_LOCAL_TZ, default America/New_York.
Blob resources answer mimeType text/plain (the template lists application/octet-stream): recorded.
trigger-long-running-operation sleeps duration/steps seconds per step and sends notifications/progress {progress:i,total:steps} only when the call carries a progressToken (recorded 0 to 10 s).

simulate-research-query requires task augmentation; tasks are per MCP session, ttl always 300000 ms whatever the client asks, stages Gathering sources / Analyzing content / Synthesizing findings / Generating report advance every ~1.0 s, completed at ~4.0 s, expire 300 s after their last update; tasks/result blocks until completion (recorded).

gzip-file-as-resource: data: URLs are decoded and compressed like Node zlib (byte-identical, OS byte 0x13); http(s) URLs: the fake is offline and serves only the recorded URLs (the default README, example.com, the GitHub 404 page); other hosts answer 'fetch failed' like an unreachable host. Session resources live per MCP session.
Session resources created by gzip-file-as-resource appear in the real resources/list; FauxCall serves resources/list from the model, so the fake's listing never shows them (resources/read does).

toggle-simulated-logging / toggle-subscriber-updates alternate Started/Stopped per MCP session and name the session id; the real server then pushes notifications every 5 s on the standalone GET stream, which the fake does not emit.

Not modeled (not listed to any client FauxCall could introspect): trigger-url-elicitation (needs elicitation.url), trigger-sampling-request-async and trigger-elicitation-request-async (need tasks.requests.* client capabilities), documented in features.md.

Capability tools (get-roots-list, trigger-elicitation-request, trigger-sampling-request) are listed just before simulate-research-query, in that order (recorded one capability at a time; the three-capability order observed in parity). For a client that declares sampling/elicitation but never answers the server's request, the real server answers isError 'MCP error -32001: Request timed out' after 60 s; get-roots-list answers at once that no roots are configured (both observed in parity runs).

URIs are normalized like new URL(): dot segments (also %2e) resolved, forbidden host code points or ports > 65535 rejected with -32603 'Invalid URL', backslash kept; template ids stop at '/' and ',' (review probes 000416-000422).
Session resources are registered under the raw URI and looked up by the normalized one, so names with spaces or dot segments can't be read back (000428-000434).

tasks/list pages 10 tasks with nextCursor = last task id of the page; cursor null -> Zod -32603; task: null on tools/call -> Zod -32603 at params.task; a task still exists 302 s after creation (expiry counts from the last update) (000439-000459).

completion/complete: invalid ref -> invalid_union with one branch per ref kind, reported together with argument issues; template variables without a completer answer without 'total' (000411-000414, parity).
A second initialize in a session gets 400 -32600 'Invalid Request: Server already initialized' on the real server (000437); FauxCall answers it.

simulate-research-query ambiguous:true from an elicitation-capable client: real task goes input_required with statusMessage 'Found multiple interpretations for "<topic>". Requesting clarification...' (parity run 3); not modeled because handlers can't see the client's declared capabilities.
